evidence: chapter-05.md scope note (exact): '(Scope: this $Q^*$ amortizes only the one‑time training + carry cost against the quality uplift; it omits the recurring per‑query prefill/retrieval saving that fine‑tuning's shorter context (§5.3(c)) would confer, so it is a lower bound on the fine‑tuning case and overstates the break‑even volume.)' The finding's own algebra matches the text's second clause: adding fine-tuning's per-query benefit to the denominator lowers Q*, so the printed Q* > true Q* = upper bound = 'overstates the break-even volume' ✓. 'a lower bound on the fine‑tuning case' bounds a different quantity (the case FOR fine-tuning, i.e. its benefit is understated) — not Q*; the two clauses are consistent (omitted benefit ⇒ understates fine-tuning's case ⇒ overstates Q*). The finding's contradiction rests on reading 'the fine-tuning case' as Q*, which is not what the phrase denotes; the note already states the upper-bound direction on the break-even volume.
